title: Wall Section Thermal Insulation Viewer with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that renders an interactive cross-section of a building wall showing thermal insulation behavior over a 24-hour day/night cycle with full time control.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use an OrthographicCamera looking at the wall cross-section from the side (camera at z=10, looking at origin).
- Ambient light (intensity 0.4) plus a directional light (intensity 0.8) from upper-left.
- The wall cross-section is built from 5 distinct layers arranged left-to-right along the X axis, each a BoxGeometry slab:
  1. Exterior Brick (width 0.5, height 4, depth 2) — color #8B4513, thermal conductivity k=0.72 W/(m·K)
  2. Air Gap (width 0.1, height 4, depth 2) — semi-transparent color #AADDFF opacity 0.3, k=0.025
  3. Insulation (width 0.3, height 4, depth 2) — color #FFD700, k=0.035
  4. Concrete Block (width 0.6, height 4, depth 2) — color #808080, k=1.4
  5. Interior Plaster (width 0.1, height 4, depth 2) — color #FAEBD7, k=0.5
- Position layers edge-to-edge starting from x=-0.8 so the full wall is centered near origin.
- Each layer mesh should have userData.layerIndex (0-4) and userData.conductivity set.

THERMAL SIMULATION:
- Simulate a 24-hour cycle. The exterior temperature follows: T_ext(h) = 20 + 15*sin((h - 6)*PI/12) °C (peaks at noon ~35°C, lowest at midnight ~5°C).
- Interior target temperature is fixed at 22°C.
- For each layer, compute a steady-state temperature at its center using a simple 1D thermal resistance model:
  - R_i = thickness_i / k_i for each layer
  - Total R = sum of all R_i
  - Temperature at the left face of layer j: T_j = T_ext - (T_ext - 22) * (sum of R_0..R_{j-1}) / R
  - Layer center temperature = average of its left and right face temperatures.
- Color each layer by blending its base color toward red (hot, >30°C) or blue (cold, <10°C) proportionally. At 22°C use the base color. Use linear interpolation.
- Show temperature gradient arrows (small ArrowHelper objects) between adjacent layers pointing from hot to cold side. Arrow length proportional to temperature difference (scale: 0.05 per °C difference). Update arrows each time step.

TIME CONTROL:
- A simulation hour variable from 0.0 to 23.99.
- DOM slider (id='timeSlider', min=0, max=23.99, step=0.01) to scrub time.
- Play/Pause button (id='playPauseBtn'). When playing, time advances at 1 simulated hour per real second, looping at 24.
- Speed control buttons: id='speedUpBtn' (doubles speed, max 8x), id='speedDownBtn' (halves speed, min 0.25x).
- Current time displayed in HUD div (id='timeDisplay') as 'HH:MM' format.
- Current speed displayed in span (id='speedDisplay').

LAYER SELECTION & DETAIL:
- Clicking on a wall layer (raycasting) selects it: add a white wireframe outline (EdgesGeometry + LineBasicMaterial white) around the selected layer.
- A detail panel (id='detailPanel') shows: layer name, thickness, conductivity, current center temperature (2 decimal places), and thermal resistance.
- Pressing keys 1-5 also selects layers 0-4 respectively.
- Pressing 'R' resets: deselects layer, sets time to 6.0, pauses, resets speed to 1x.

INSULATION TOGGLE:
- A checkbox (id='insulationToggle') labeled 'Remove Insulation'. When checked, set insulation layer conductivity to 0.72 (same as brick, simulating no insulation) and change its color to match brick. Recalculate all temperatures immediately.
- When unchecked, restore original insulation properties.

ENERGY TRACKING:
- Continuously compute heat flux Q = (T_ext - 22) / R_total in W/m². Track cumulative energy over simulated time: E += |Q| * dt (in Wh/m²).
- Display current Q in span (id='heatFluxDisplay') and cumulative E in span (id='energyDisplay'), both to 2 decimal places.
- The cumulative energy must reset to 0 when 'R' is pressed.

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- simulationHour: number (0-23.99)
- isPlaying: boolean
- playbackSpeed: number
- exteriorTemp: number (current T_ext)
- interiorTemp: 22 (constant)
- layerTemperatures: array of 5 numbers (center temps)
- layerConductivities: array of 5 numbers
- layerResistances: array of 5 numbers (R_i for each layer)
- totalResistance: number
- selectedLayerIndex: number or -1 if none
- insulationRemoved: boolean
- heatFlux: number (current Q)
- cumulativeEnergy: number
- arrowCount: number (should be 4, one between each adjacent pair)
- layerCount: 5
- temperatureGradients: array of 4 numbers (temp difference between adjacent layer centers, left minus right)

All numerical state values must be updated every frame. Ensure no NaN values ever appear in state.
physics_constraints: 1D steady-state heat conduction: T(x) linear within each layer. Total thermal resistance R = sum(thickness_i / k_i). Heat flux Q = deltaT / R. Temperature at layer boundaries computed via cumulative resistance fraction. Energy conservation: cumulative energy is time-integral of |Q|. Exterior temperature follows sinusoidal diurnal cycle T_ext = 20 + 15*sin((h-6)*PI/12).
